title: Lucy Guo says supporting her ex cost her $1 billion in Anthropic gains
excerpt: Investor Sarah Guo said she passed on an early Anthropic investment to support her ex-girlfriend. "Love makes you dumb," she said. "Stay single."
content_html:
Scale AI cofounder says she passed on an Anthropic investment to support her ex's lifestyle: 'Lost a billion'

By Henry Chandonnet

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-21T12:00:02.491Z

We do crazy things for love — in Lucy Guo's case, she says that includes passing on an Anthropic investment that could've netted a billion dollars.

Guo has several titles. She's the cofounder of Scale AI, which also minted Meta's mullet-in-chief, Alexandr Wang. She's an investor through her venture capital firm, Backend Capital. And she's a DJ, too, opening for fellow investor Diplo.

On the day of Anthropic's IPO, one title was top of mind: ex-girlfriend.

"If you ever feel stupid, just know that I didn't invest in Anthropic at $183B because I wanted to continue supporting my ex's lifestyle," Guo wrote on X. Guo advised people to "stay single," explaining that she "lost a billion dollars over this one."

Don't worry: Guo says she still had a nice payday. The VC said her seed investment landed nine figures of Anthropic stock. According to a later post, Anthropic also "forgot" to make her sign a lockup agreement. Anthropic didn't respond to a request for comment from Business Insider.

She did not say which ex her X post was about. Anthropic's Series F, which valued it at the $183 billion Guo referenced, was announced in September 2025. In court documents, Guo has said that she dated British model Wallis Day from July 2025 to February 2026.

Guo released a breakup track titled "Done With Your Ex" in May. In November, she filed a court application seeking to subpoena Meta in relation to Day's Instagram post from the month the song was released.

According to court documents, Day wrote that Guo was "dangerous," and accused her of misconduct related to theft, and coercion to sign an NDA, and denial of emergency service access to her home due to the presence of drugs.

Guo said that the post was "replete with falsehoods," specifically denying the emergency services claim. She said that she planned to file a defamation claim against Day in the United Kingdom.

The application for a subpoena is ongoing, and Guo does not appear to have yet filed a defamation suit in the UK. Representatives for Guo declined to comment. Representatives for Day did not respond to requests for comment from Business Insider.

The reaction to Guo's post was mixed. Some called it "ragebait" or a "humble brag." Another user said that posts like Guo's guaranteed that a wealth tax would eventually pass in California.

Guo's Anthropic investment woes seem to be inspiring her creativity. On Thursday, she posted a video of a "rough draft" of a new song, saying that she was turning her billion-dollar missed opportunity into a "banger."

The song's title: "Love with a Salary."

Guo's Anthropic investment woes seem to be inspiring her creativity. On Thursday, she posted a video of a "rough draft" of a new song, saying that she was turning her billion-dollar missed opportunity into a "banger."

The song's title: "Love with a Salary."
